title: San Marino score after 8.3 seconds against England
angle: Davide Gualtieri scored 8.3 seconds after kick-off in Bologna (England still won 7-1), and he was a part-timer who later worked as a computer salesman (Wikipedia) / ran an electronics shop (UEFA).

title: Ferenc Puskás dies in Budapest aged 79
angle: Puskás scored four of Real Madrid's seven goals in the 1960 European Cup final, and later played four matches for Spain after becoming a Spanish citizen in 1962.

title: Henry handball sends France to the World Cup, eliminating Ireland
angle: The Football Association of Ireland was reportedly paid EUR 5 million by FIFA after the handball, according to the Irish Times, which says the sum surfaced in 2014 and was later confirmed by FAI chief John Delaney.

title: Pelé scores his 1,000th career goal at the Maracanã
angle: The 1,000th goal was a penalty against Vasco da Gama at the Maracanã, and Brazil's postal service issued a commemorative stamp for it.

title: Ronaldinho gets a standing ovation at the Bernabéu
angle: Ronaldinho scored twice in a 3-0 win and Real Madrid fans stood to applaud him; the only other Barcelona player the Wikipedia article names with that tribute at the Bernabéu is Diego Maradona.

title: Qatar lose the World Cup opener to Ecuador
angle: Qatar became the first host nation to lose the opening match of a World Cup, and Valencia had a goal ruled out for offside by VAR in the opening minutes before scoring twice.

title: Saudi Arabia beat Argentina at the World Cup
angle: Argentina had three first-half goals ruled out for marginal offsides before losing, ending a 36-match unbeaten run.

title: Pig's head thrown at Luís Figo at the Camp Nou
angle: Barcelona 0-0 Real Madrid was stopped for a long spell as fans threw objects at Figo; teammate Michel Salgado recalled coins, a knife and a whisky bottle among the missiles.

title: Hungary beat England 6-3 at Wembley
angle: Hidegkuti scored a hat-trick, the first within a minute of kick-off, and Puskás's sole-of-the-boot drag-back left England captain Billy Wright chasing empty space before his goal.

title: George Best dies aged 59
angle: Best scored six goals in an 8-2 FA Cup win over Northampton Town in 1970, and Glentoran had earlier rejected him as too small and light.

title: Diego Maradona dies aged 60
angle: Nine days after his death, on 4 December 2020, Napoli's stadium was renamed the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona.

title: Chapecoense plane crash near Medellín
angle: Atlético Nacional asked CONMEBOL to award Chapecoense the Copa Sudamericana, which was done on 5 December 2016, and Nacional received a Fair Play award for it.

title: Barcelona 5-0 Real Madrid at the Camp Nou
angle: The Clásico was moved to a Monday because Catalonia held parliamentary elections the day before; Villa scored twice and Madrid had been unbeaten that season.

title: Scotland and England play the first international
angle: The 0-0 draw at Hamilton Crescent used tape as the crossbar and all eleven Scotland players came from Queen's Park.

title: Lionel Messi wins his first Ballon d'Or
angle: Messi took 473 points to Ronaldo's 233, a record 240-point margin at the time.

title: Messi wins a record sixth Ballon d'Or
angle: Messi beat Virgil van Dijk by just 7 points (686 to 679), with Ronaldo third on 476.

title: Luka Modrić wins the Ballon d'Or, ending the Messi-Ronaldo run
angle: Messi finished only fifth, his first finish outside the top three since 2006, and Kaká in 2007 was the last winner before Modrić who was not Messi or Ronaldo.

title: Morocco beat Spain on penalties in the World Cup round of 16
angle: Spain scored none of their three shootout penalties (Morocco won 3-0), and Morocco's goalkeeper Yassine Bounou had made just one save in open play over 120 minutes.

title: Juventus win the Intercontinental Cup on penalties vs Argentinos Juniors
angle: The win made Juventus the first club to win every official continental competition plus the world title, and Platini scored the decisive penalty.

title: Messi scores his 86th goal of 2012, breaking Gerd Muller's calendar-year record
angle: Muller's record of 85 goals (set in 1972) had stood for about 40 years; Messi, 25, passed it with a double at Real Betis, 74 goals for Barcelona and 12 for Argentina.

title: Morocco beat Portugal to become the first African World Cup semi-finalist
angle: Morocco became the first African and Arab nation to reach a World Cup semi-final, winning 1-0 on a header from Youssef En-Nesyri just before half-time.

title: Flamengo beat Liverpool 3-0 in the Intercontinental Cup in Tokyo
angle: It was Liverpool's first Intercontinental Cup appearance: they had declined to play in 1977 and 1978.

title: River Plate beat Steaua Bucharest 1-0 to win the Intercontinental Cup
angle: The Tokyo final kicked off at 4 a.m. Romanian time so it was not shown live in Romania, and Norberto Alonso retired after it, his last match as a player.

title: The Bosman ruling at the European Court of Justice
angle: Bosman's wages at Liege were cut by roughly 70-75% when he was frozen out, and he received about 312,000 pounds in compensation in 1998.

title: Internacional beat Barcelona 1-0 in the Club World Cup final
angle: Substitute Adriano Gabiru scored the 82nd-minute winner, and Barcelona's Deco won the tournament's Golden Ball despite losing the final.

title: Barcelona beat Santos 4-0 in the Club World Cup final
angle: Neymar, then 19, was largely held quiet in the final, and Barcelona had lost striker David Villa to a fractured shin in the semi-final.

title: Cristiano Ronaldo hat-trick wins Real Madrid the Club World Cup vs Kashima Antlers
angle: Ronaldo was the first player to score a hat-trick in a Club World Cup final, and Kashima's Gaku Shibasaki scored twice to force extra time at 2-2.

title: Argentina beat France on penalties in the World Cup final
angle: Mbappe became only the second man to score a hat-trick in a World Cup final, after Geoff Hurst in 1966, yet ended on the losing side.

title: Barcelona win a record sixth trophy of the year at the Club World Cup
angle: Barcelona were still losing until Pedro equalised about a minute from the end of normal time; Messi's 110th-minute winner gave them six trophies in one calendar year, beating Liverpool's five in 2001.

title: Manchester United win the Club World Cup with ten men
angle: Nemanja Vidic was sent off soon after half-time, and Wayne Rooney scored the 73rd-minute winner against LDU Quito.

title: The Christmas Truce football on the Western Front
angle: The photo most often shown as the 1914 truce match was actually taken near Thessaloniki, Greece, in 1915, and the most detailed match account (Germans beat Scots 3-2) comes from a German regiment's own history.

title: 66 goals in ten First Division matches on Boxing Day
angle: Fulham beat Ipswich 10-1 (Graham Leggat scored four), and two days later Manchester United beat Burnley 5-1 in the return, avenging a 6-1 Boxing Day defeat, with George Best scoring his first United goal.

title: Pele dies aged 82
angle: Pele died at Sao Paulo's Albert Einstein hospital at 3:27pm local time; he is the only player to win three World Cups and Brazil's all-time top scorer with 77 goals in 92 games.

title: Stanley Matthews is knighted while still playing
angle: He was knighted in the 1965 New Year Honours and played his last League game on 6 February 1965, five days after turning 50, the oldest player in England's top flight.

title: Ibrox disaster at the Old Firm match
angle: A 1974 Glasgow sheriff court ruling found Rangers at fault for the crush that killed 66 people, and Rangers did not dispute the finding, only the damages.

title: Ronaldo unveiled by Al Nassr in Riyadh
angle: The deal was agreed on 30 December 2022, he was presented at 25,000-capacity Mrsool Park on 3 January, and debuted on 22 January 2023 in a 1-0 win over Al-Ettifaq.

title: Eusebio dies in Lisbon
angle: Before he played a game for Benfica in 1961 he was sent to Lagos in the Algarve, reportedly for fear of Sporting CP interfering, while the clubs disputed his transfer.

title: Mario Zagallo dies aged 92
angle: In 1970 he became the first person to win the World Cup as both player and manager, a feat later matched by Beckenbauer and Deschamps.

title: Brian Clough appointed Nottingham Forest manager
angle: Forest were 13th in the Second Division and nearly bankrupt when he arrived, and his first game in charge was a 1-0 FA Cup replay win over Tottenham, Neil Martin scoring.

title: Gianluca Vialli dies aged 58
angle: At 33 years 308 days he won the 1998 Cup Winners' Cup as Chelsea player-manager, the youngest manager to win a UEFA competition at the time (record stood until 2011).

title: Messi wins fourth straight Ballon d'Or
angle: He took 41.60% of the vote to Ronaldo's 23.68%, becoming the first player to win four Ballon d'Ors, and four in a row.

title: Franz Beckenbauer dies aged 78
angle: The popular story behind the nickname 'Der Kaiser' is probably untrue; a Welt am Sonntag report traces it to the 1969 cup final foul on Schalke's Reinhard Libuda.

title: Togo team bus attacked in Cabinda before Africa Cup of Nations
angle: After the government recalled the team, CAF banned Togo from the next two Africa Cup of Nations and fined it 50,000 US dollars.

title: Thierry Henry scores winner on second Arsenal debut
angle: Coming off the bench on a two-month loan from New York Red Bulls, he scored in the 78th minute against Leeds in the FA Cup, extending his Arsenal club record to 227 goals.

title: Ronaldo wins the first Best FIFA Men's Player award
angle: The Puskas Award that night went to Mohd Faiz Subri for a goal in a 2016 Malaysia Super League match between Penang and Pahang.

title: Beckham announces move to LA Galaxy
angle: The widely reported 250 million dollar value was a publicity figure for his total earnings; the Galaxy contract itself was 32.5 million dollars over five years.

title: Messi wins fifth Ballon d'Or
angle: It was the last edition of the joint France Football and FIFA Ballon d'Or; Messi took 41.33%, Ronaldo 27.76%, Neymar 7.86%.

title: Sven-Goran Eriksson starts as England manager
angle: He had agreed in October 2000 to start in June 2001, but Lazio asked him to resign in January so he began early, as England's first foreign manager.

title: Ronaldo wins third Ballon d'Or
angle: Messi finished second by just 0.04 percentage points over Manuel Neuer (15.76% to 15.72%), behind Ronaldo's 37.66%.

title: Ronaldo ends Messi's run with second Ballon d'Or
angle: Ronaldo scored 69 goals in 60 appearances in 2013 to Messi's 45 in 46, and Pele received an honorary Ballon d'Or at the same ceremony.

title: Erling Haaland scores a hat-trick on his Borussia Dortmund debut at Augsburg
angle: He came on in the 56th minute with Dortmund 3-1 down and completed the treble in the 79th, the first Bundesliga debut hat-trick since Aubameyang's, also at Augsburg for Dortmund.

title: Garrincha dies in Rio de Janeiro aged 49
angle: He was born with his right leg about 6 cm shorter than his left, and a doctor once certified him as crippled as a child.

title: Sir Matt Busby dies, aged 84
angle: After the 1958 Munich air crash he received the last rites twice and only learned of Duncan Edwards's death about three weeks later.

title: Emiliano Sala's plane disappears over the English Channel two days after he joined Cardiff City
angle: A privately funded search found the wreckage on the seabed on 3 February 2019, after the official search had been called off.

title: Eusebio is born in Lourenco Marques, Mozambique
angle: Benfica signed him in 1960 in secret under the code name "Ruth Malosso" while Sporting CP claimed rights to him.

title: Eric Cantona's kung-fu kick at Selhurst Park
angle: The fan he kicked, Matthew Simmons, was later fined 500 pounds and banned from the stadium for a year, and Cantona's own punishment was cut on appeal from two weeks in prison to 120 hours of community service.

title: Sky Sports sacks Andy Gray over sexist off-air comments about assistant referee Sian Massey
angle: Sky said its decision came after new evidence of an off-air incident from December 2010, not only the Massey tape.

title: Gianluigi Buffon is born in Carrara
angle: He began as an outfield midfielder at Parma and switched to goalkeeper after an injury crisis, inspired by Thomas N'Kono at the 1990 World Cup.

title: Romario is born in Rio de Janeiro
angle: His celebrated 1,000th goal (20 May 2007, a penalty for Vasco) counts friendlies and youth games, and the official tallies cited by sources are lower (FIFA 760 per Goal, 929 per Wikipedia, so quote carefully).

title: Japan beat Australia 1-0 in the Asian Cup final after extra time
angle: Substitute Tadanari Lee scored a volley in the 109th minute from a Yuto Nagatomo cross, giving Japan a record fourth Asian Cup.

title: Fernando Torres joins Chelsea from Liverpool for a reported 50 million pounds
angle: Liverpool could only accept the bid after finishing the Andy Carroll signing just before the 11pm deadline, and Torres then went 903 minutes before his first Chelsea goal.

title: Luis Suarez signs for Liverpool from Ajax
angle: He was Liverpool's record signing for only a few hours: Andy Carroll signed for 35 million pounds later that day, against Suarez's reported 22.8 million, and Suarez scored on his debut two days later.

title: Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang joins Arsenal from Dortmund for a club-record fee
angle: He was Arsenal's third signing of that January window, after Mavropanos and Mkhitaryan, and debuted three days later in a 5-1 win over Everton, scoring the fourth goal.

title: Enzo Fernandez joins Chelsea from Benfica for a British-record 106.8 million pounds
angle: Benfica had signed him only about six months earlier for roughly 10 million.
